meta.description: Download raw sequencing reads from NCBI SRA using sra-tools (prefetch, fasterq-dump, vdb-validate) or the ENA mirror. Use when pulling FASTQ for SRR/ERR/DRR accessions, deciding between SRA-direct, ENA mirror, or AWS/GCP cloud mirror (STRIDES), handling --include-technical for 10x and other single-cell records, validating with MD5/vdb-validate, navigating SRR/SRX/SRS/SRP/PRJNA hierarchy, or finding accessions via pysradb.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOIs/PMIDs/p-values/sample sizes in any output; the Skill only moves real, verifiable sequencing data and does not generate scientific claims.

practice_boundaries.detail: No diagnostic or prescriptive medical conclusions in any output; Input 6 exposed a data-access gap, not a medical-advice violation.

methodological_ground.detail: SKILL.md and usage-guide.md never mention dbGaP, controlled access, authorization, consent, IRB, or ethical-compliance requirements anywhere (confirmed by grep across both files, zero matches), despite SRA routinely hosting dbGaP-controlled human genomic data directly within this Skill's own stated scope. Input 6 confirmed an agent following the Skill would attempt a controlled-access accession exactly like a public one, with no guidance on the --ngc mechanism or on stopping to ask for authorization.

code_usability.detail: SKILL.md's own 'preferred default' ENA-mirror snippet and examples/download_batch.sh both contain a reproducible off-by-one column-index bug (assume fields=fastq_ftp,fastq_md5 map to columns 1,2; ENA's filereport API always prepends run_accession as column 1, shifting real data to columns 2,3). Confirmed failing 100% of the time (4/4 real accessions across Inputs 1, 5, 7) as shipped; a one-line index fix (cut -f2/-f3) restores 100% success on the identical accessions.

functional_suitability.note: Broad, accurate coverage of SRA-toolkit, ENA, STRIDES, 10x and accession-hierarchy use cases (Completeness 3/4), but the flagship ENA-mirror code pattern is factually broken (Correctness 1/4) and the ENA-vs-SRA-direct 'interchangeable' framing is demonstrably imprecise; approach itself is well-matched to the task (Appropriateness 3/4).

reliability.note: The ENA path fails loudly rather than silently, but with a misleading error ('Could not resolve host') that misattributes a parsing bug as a network issue; no structured recovery guidance for that failure mode.

performance_context.note: 372-line single-file SKILL.md with no references/ layering (all content loads at once, though within the 500-line guideline); per-path workflows themselves are linear and minimal.

agent_usability.note: Strong 'Failure modes'/'Common errors' sections proactively document several real traps (max-size, scratch overhead, 10x, Aspera) that were independently confirmed accurate, but the skill's own worst defect (the ENA column bug) and the controlled-access gap are not among them.

human_usability.note: Description and code patterns closely match how a researcher would actually phrase these requests (4/4 Discoverability); the ENA failure mode is not a graceful strict-rejection, it is a misleading unexplained error (1/4 Forgiveness).

security.note: No hardcoded secrets, all documented paths are public/unauthenticated; accession strings are quoted (not eval'd) throughout so injection risk is low, but no explicit format validation exists before interpolating accessions into curl/prefetch commands.

maintainability.note: Scripts are small, isolated and easy to patch (the ENA bug's real-world fix is a one-line change); good observable pass/fail behavior made this defect independently discoverable through execution alone.

agent_specific.note: Precise, detailed trigger description (4/4) and explicit 'Related Skills' composability (4/4); no escape hatch anywhere for controlled-access data or for confirming large/costly downloads before starting them (1/4 Escape Hatches).

key_strengths: SRA-toolkit path (prefetch + vdb-validate + fasterq-dump) is fully correct and verified against three independent ground-truth sources: 14,052 spots matching vdb-dump --info, Entrez efetch runinfo, and raw FASTQ line counts exactly.
pysradb-based accession resolution (BioProject -> SRR) works correctly out of the box and matches an independently confirmed real-world count (6,508 runs for PRJEB37378).

The 'Failure modes' and 'Common errors' sections proactively document several real, non-obvious traps (prefetch --max-size default, fasterq-dump scratch overhead, 10x --include-technical, Aspera deprecation) that were independently confirmed accurate against the real tools.

download_batch.sh's per-accession error handling (continue-on-failure, failed.txt tracking, accurate summary counts) is sound engineering that works correctly once the underlying column-index bug is fixed -- confirmed by a one-line patch reaching 3/3 real downloads.

recommendations.title: ENA-mirror download code is broken (off-by-one column bug)
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's 'preferred default' ENA-mirror snippet and examples/download_batch.sh both assume ENA's filereport TSV columns are (1=fastq_ftp, 2=fastq_md5), but ENA always prepends run_accession as column 1, shifting the real data to columns 2 and 3 (and column 4 for download_batch.sh's extra read_count field). Fails 100% of the time (4/4 real accessions tested) as shipped.
recommendations.root_cause: The cut -f1/-f2 indices were written without accounting for ENA's fixed leading run_accession column.
recommendations.fix: In SKILL.md's inline snippet, change URLS to cut -f2 and MD5S to cut -f3. In examples/download_batch.sh, apply the same one-column shift (URLS=cut -f2, MD5S=cut -f3). Confirmed: this one-line fix in each file restores 100% success (3/3 real accessions, MD5-verified) with no other change needed.

recommendations.title: No guidance for controlled-access (dbGaP) human data
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md/usage-guide.md never mention dbGaP, controlled access, authorization, consent, or ethical-compliance requirements, despite SRA routinely hosting dbGaP-restricted human genomic data within this Skill's own stated scope. An agent following the Skill would attempt the same prefetch/ENA calls on a restricted accession with no guidance on interpreting the resulting authorization failure or on the --ngc repository-key mechanism.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill was authored and exemplified entirely around public bacterial/model-organism data and never accounted for the controlled-access branch of its own domain.
recommendations.fix: Add a short 'Controlled-access data' section: how to recognize a dbGaP-gated accession, the --ngc <repository-key>.ngc prefetch flag, and an explicit instruction to stop and ask the user for authorization/DUA status before attempting a download of a human accession outside a known-public study.

recommendations.title: download scripts call pigz with no Windows fallback
recommendations.problem: download_single.sh, download_batch.sh and prefetch_large.sh all call pigz directly; pigz has no official Windows build, so these scripts fail at the compression step on a bare Windows shell after the download/extraction already succeeded.
recommendations.root_cause: Scripts assume a Linux/WSL/conda execution environment.
recommendations.fix: Detect pigz availability and fall back to gzip (already noted as functionally equivalent, just single-threaded, in usage-guide.md's Tips) or state the WSL/conda requirement explicitly in Required Setup.

recommendations.title: ENA mirror and SRA-direct are not actually interchangeable
recommendations.problem: For the real test accession, ENA's mirror FASTQ has 13,911 read pairs vs. NCBI SRA-direct's 14,052 -- a 141-pair (~1%) discrepancy confirmed via independent ground truth and matching MD5s (not a corrupt download). SKILL.md presents these sources as freely substitutable for 'the same' run.
recommendations.root_cause: ENA independently re-calls FASTQ from resubmitted BAM/CRAM rather than mirroring NCBI's SRA-format bytes; SKILL.md doesn't mention this cross-archive harmonization difference.
recommendations.fix: Add a note that ENA and SRA-direct read counts can differ slightly for the same accession, and that a pipeline should not validate a downloaded FASTQ's read count against a count obtained from the other source.

recommendations.title: Documented size-check mitigation doesn't work as stated
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md tells users to 'query metadata first with pysradb metadata' to avoid the --max-size trap, but pysradb's detailed metadata has no byte-size column; the real check requires ENA's portal API fastq_bytes field.
recommendations.root_cause: The suggested mitigation was never verified against pysradb's actual output columns.
recommendations.fix: Point users to the ENA portal API's fields=fastq_bytes query (or sra-stat --xml) for pre-download size checks instead of, or in addition to, pysradb metadata.

recommendations.title: No confirmation step before large downloads
recommendations.problem: The Skill will generate a --max-size 200G command for any large run without prompting the user to confirm a many-GB pull is wanted, compounding the existing STRIDES cross-region egress-cost warning already present elsewhere in SKILL.md.
recommendations.root_cause: Escape Hatches is the weakest static-score dimension for this Skill; no stop-and-confirm guidance exists for large or ambiguous requests.
recommendations.fix: Add an instruction for the agent to state the expected download size/time and get explicit user confirmation before starting any prefetch/fasterq-dump above a stated threshold (e.g. 10 GB).
